PullRequest.Title: chat: send device file attachments to cloud sandboxes
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

## What changed

A local file attached to a cloud sandbox conversation could appear in the prompt as a `file://` link the agent could not open. VS Code now sends the contents of explicitly attached device files using AHP's existing embedded-resource format, with no cloud-specific extension allowlist. Sandbox files remain URI references and image handling is unchanged.

Initial and queued messages use the same preparation. A selection includes only the selected text. Excluded, unreadable, or oversized device files fail before submission; device file snapshots share a 16 MiB budget per message.

## How to test

1. Create a local CSV outside the repository with a distinctive value. Attach it to a new cloud sandbox session and ask for that value without including it in the prompt.
2. In a follow-up, attach a local binary file with an unrecognized extension and ask the agent to report its byte count or checksum. Compare it with the original.
3. Attach an excluded file or exceed the combined 16 MiB limit. Verify that VS Code identifies the file and does not submit the request.

## Validation

- 14 focused tests passed in standalone Mocha and DOM test harnesses. Targeted TypeScript diagnostics passed for all 16 changed TypeScript files.
- `git diff HEAD^ HEAD --check` passed.
- `pnpm run compile-client` and the standard Electron test runner were blocked by missing dependencies after `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` failed to fetch packages. Not yet tested against a deployed cloud sandbox.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The unloaded-selection trigger, strong manager retention, absent success-path disposal, and existing reference-counted cleanup mechanism are explicit in the traced code. Only the number and size of files users attach are uncertain.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Full text-file models, text buffers, and model listeners retained in the long-lived TextFileEditorModelManager.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: One retained model per distinct previously unloaded selected file, potentially across many messages. Retention scales with whole source-file sizes, not selection sizes or the 16 MiB message limit; already loaded models are reused.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Accumulating renderer memory and associated GC/model-service overhead throughout the window lifetime.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The submission path passed selection locations through as URI/range attachments; it did not create an unowned client text-file model during snapshot preparation.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Preparing a selected file whose editor model is not loaded now directly resolves a full TextFileEditorModel and retains no disposable reference or cleanup handle.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The newly added fallback at line 60 calls this.textFileService.files.resolve(uri), extracts textEditorModel, and never releases the resolved model after textSnapshot or on failure.
Findings.Title: Release text models resolved only to snapshot a selection
Findings.Impact: Sending selections from closed files keeps the full source buffers and associated editor models alive after submission or chat closure. Repeating this with distinct files accumulates renderer memory even when only a few selected lines were sent.
Findings.Evidence: Selections can be attached without opening their files through chatContextActions.ts:349-360, or their editor can be closed before submission; ChatAttachmentModel.asFileVariableEntry retains only uri/range (chatAttachmentModel.ts:189-196). TextFileEditorModelManager.doResolve creates/registers a model and stores it in mapResourceToModel; successful resolution leaves it there (textFileEditorModelManager.ts:429-448,458-488,537-550). Its automatic disposal only handles failed resolution, not successful snapshot extraction. ResourceModelCollection provides the existing lifecycle-safe alternative: createModelReference resolves the shared file model and destroyReferencedObject waits for canDispose before disposing it (services/textmodelResolver/common/textModelResolverService.ts:76-80,132-167). No cleanup in prepare releases the directly resolved model, including when a later attachment fails.
Findings.Recommendation: Acquire a scoped ITextModelService.createModelReference when resolution is needed and dispose that reference in finally after capturing the selection, preserving ownership of models already held by editors.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The newly awaited call, unrestricted file-picker route, unbuffered preference, parallel validation, and uncancellable regular-file native read are all traced in repository code. Exact memory duration and frequency of oversized attachments are unmeasured.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Bytes read from disk and the full-file native buffer allocated by the local filesystem process.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: One unbuffered read for each newly captured clean file, processed serially until the first failure; the offending read scales with the entire file size, not the remaining per-message budget. Existing snapshots skip the content read.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Large transient memory pressure and excessive disk I/O, potentially exhausting filesystem-process memory on very large attachments.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Cloud submissions did not perform this local snapshot read; files were represented by URI references, and the cloud file picker was restricted to images.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Submitting a clean device-file attachment now calls IFileService.readFile before request acceptance, relying on limits.size to prevent oversized reads.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The new prepare() implementation adds fileService.readFile(uri, { limits: { size: remaining } }, token) at line 68, and chatServiceImpl.ts:1674 awaits prepare() for cloud submissions. Cloud registrations also newly enable unrestricted file attachments.
Findings.Title: Bound the filesystem read before allocating oversized attachments
Findings.Impact: Attaching an oversized dataset, archive, or binary can consume hundreds of MiB or GiB of filesystem-process memory and disk I/O merely to reject the message, despite the advertised 16 MiB budget.
Findings.Evidence: FileService.doReadFile sets preferUnbuffered: true (src/vs/platform/files/common/fileService.ts:558-573). doReadFileStream starts the content read alongside validateReadFile rather than awaiting its size check, and readFileUnbuffered passes no size limit to provider.readFile (:604-641, :701-728). For local files, DiskFileSystemProviderClient.readFile sends a readFile IPC; DiskFileSystemProvider.readFile uses Promises.readFile(fd) for regular files and does not consult the cancellation token (src/vs/platform/files/node/diskFileSystemProvider.ts:223-243). Thus even when the parallel stat rejects the attachment, an already-issued native read still reads and allocates the entire file. The existing readFileStream path instead checks limits incrementally through files/common/io.ts:91-95,122-125.
Findings.Recommendation: Use the existing bounded readFileStream path and buffer only its size-limited output; optionally reject from a preliminary stat as well. Do not rely on readFile's parallel metadata validation to bound allocation.

Scenarios.Scenario: Submit clean device files or arbitrary binaries to an existing cloud conversation, including an oversized attachment.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: sendRequestInternal awaits prepare before accepting the request, creating its response, or queueing it. Each eligible file is checked for exclusion, read, and base64-encoded before the AHP turn or pending-message action can be sent. Oversized files abort preparation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Pick files, stat each selected resource, and construct URI-based attachment entries without reading non-image content.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One picker interaction and approximately one resource stat per selected non-image file.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Cloud capability registrations did not advertise file attachments, so this picker was restricted to images. The shared picker/resolver implementation itself is unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs while attaching files, before submission; does not enforce the new submission budget.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Ask the registered ignored-file provider through extension-host RPC whether each URI is excluded.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One awaited provider check per eligible file entry with a URI when a provider exists; no provider means immediate false. prepare itself has no cache.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This submission path did not perform these explicit snapshot exclusion checks.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Serialized within prepare and blocks submission before each content read.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Stat and unbuffered-read a clean local file; local filesystem calls cross DiskFileSystemProviderClient IPC.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One content read and metadata validation per newly captured clean file, serial across entries until failure. Already captured snapshots skip content reads. The first rejected oversized file can still cause one full native read.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No local submission-time snapshot read; file entries were converted to URI references.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Successful reads block request acceptance; rejected oversized reads can continue consuming filesystem-process resources because regular-file native reads ignore cancellation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Encode new file bytes to base64 and place them in embedded-resource attachments.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One encoding per newly captured file; total successful raw bytes capped at 16 MiB and base64 is approximately four thirds that size. Existing snapshots reuse their string.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Clean device files supplied URI metadata rather than embedded bytes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Encoding completes on the submission path before dispatch.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send the existing AHP turn action through the connection transport, now including all embedded file attachments in the same logical message.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One logical turn dispatch containing the attachment collection, not one network request per file. Transport framing may split the payload.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same dispatch boundary existed, but these files supplied URI references instead of base64 payloads.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Remote agent cannot use the submitted files until the action arrives.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Repository host implementation decodes embedded resources and writes attachment snapshots, replacing them with host resource references.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One write per embedded attachment, concurrently scheduled with Promise.all for the message.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same rewrite machinery already handled embedded images and resource snapshots; this PR supplies device-file bytes instead of relying on reverse resource reads.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The host rewrite precedes action processing; deployed cloud-host implementation was not available to inspect.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: F explicit file entries across attachedContext and resolvedVariables; ordinary widget attachments are deduplicated by attachment ID, but prepare adds no further deduplication. Successful captured bytes total at most 16 MiB. One oversized file can be arbitrarily larger than that budget.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: prepare processes entries serially, with one exclusion check then one content operation per entry. FileService internally overlaps stat and unbuffered read; there is no shared prepare limiter across independent submissions. Host attachment rewrite uses Promise.all.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Fresh clean files are read even if the operating-system disk cache is warm. Existing entry.snapshot values bypass content reads and encoding but still undergo URI-based exclusion checks and budget accounting. There is no newly introduced cross-file or cross-message content cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced the capability flag, awaited preparation, unbuffered FileService implementation, local filesystem IPC, native read, attachment conversion, and dispatch.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual attachment sizes, disk speeds, and filesystem-process memory headroom are unmeasured. Deployment-specific cloud transport and host timings are unknown.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported the unbounded native read behind the nominal size limit. Successful bounded reads, required encoding, and the larger single dispatch are expected costs of sending file contents, not separate findings.

Scenarios.Scenario: Submit a selection from a file whose editor is closed or was never opened, including selections attached from search results.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: prepare resolves an unloaded source file into a full text-file model, obtains selected text, and encodes it before submission. An existing model avoids the resolution step.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve a text-file model, checking working-copy backup state and otherwise reading/decoding the source through textFileService.readStream.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One cold full-model resolution per distinct unloaded source URI; loaded models are reused, and TextFileEditorModelManager joins pending resolves by resource.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The submission path passed URI/range selection attachments through without creating client text-file models for snapshot extraction.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Resolution must finish before the selected text can be captured.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Check file exclusion through the registered extension-host provider.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One provider call per selected-file entry with a URI, if registered; entries are processed serially.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No snapshot-preparation exclusion call on this submission path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Completes before model resolution or selection extraction.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Include only captured selected text in the existing AHP action.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One grouped turn or pending-message dispatch, not one per selected file.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same boundary carried selection URI/range references.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: U distinct previously unloaded selected files; selected bytes share the 16 MiB message budget, but source-file model sizes are not bounded by the selection sizes.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Selections are prepared serially. Model manager coalesces in-flight resolution per URI but provides no automatic success-path disposal. Full buffers remain strongly owned by its resource map.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm loaded text models avoid source reads. Cold direct files.resolve inserts a model into the long-lived manager; it is not a disposable reference and successful capture never releases it. Subsequent uses of that URI reuse the retained model.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: search-result attachment creation, URI/range-only attachment storage, full-model creation and map ownership, absence of release, and the existing scoped model-reference alternative were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number and size of closed files selected across messages are unknown. Retention and its whole-file scaling are explicit and do not depend on profiling.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported missing cleanup of models resolved solely for selection capture. Required reading and decoding for a cold selection are not separately reported.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create a new cloud sandbox from a draft carrying device-file attachments.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Snapshot preparation now finishes before the initial draft request is accepted. Existing provisioning, session-type availability, configuration validation, naming, and draft commit follow. _sendFirstTurn submits the captured attachments on the committed session.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Capture device-file bytes or selections before beginning the draft workflow.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One cold content operation per eligible new file, serially; the committed-session resend reuses snapshots rather than rereading their contents.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No local device-file snapshot preparation before draft provisioning.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Intentionally prevents provisioning/submission with excluded, unreadable, or oversized device attachments.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Provision a sandbox, await its connection/session type, resolve session configuration, optionally validate model configuration, and rename the task.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing per-draft operations; optional calls depend on configuration, not file count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same provisioning and validation sequence already ran.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing startup barrier after successful attachment preparation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: The committed-session send rechecks exclusions for captured entries that retain a URI.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most another provider check per URI-bearing file; existing snapshots incur no second file-content read or base64 encoding.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No file snapshot checks; only existing image variables were forwarded as resolved variables.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send the first actual agent turn on the committed session with all attachments grouped into its action.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One logical first-turn dispatch after provisioning.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same forwarding path existed for prompt and image attachments; this diff also preserves resolved file entries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Remote agent starts only after commit and this dispatch.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: F attached device files and any resolved file variables, with a combined 16 MiB raw snapshot budget. One draft provisioning flow per new sandbox; no per-file provisioning fan-out.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: File preparation is serial within each submission; the existing draft provisioning flow and first-turn forwarding are awaited in order. Separate draft sessions are not globally serialized by this change.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Snapshots created on the draft are reused on committed-session submission. Existing configuration and connection caches are not changed. No evidence of repeated cold file-content reads during normal draft handoff.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Cloud provisioning and network durations are environment-dependent and unmeasured; deployment behavior cannot be confirmed from this repository alone.
Scenarios.Verdict: The two reported preparation issues also apply here. Moving attachment validation before costly provisioning is intentional and is not reported as an independent latency regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Queue or steer a cloud follow-up and reuse captured attachments on later submission or restored history.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Preparation completes before queue acceptance. The agent-host handler converts pending variables to attachments and diffs messages before dispatch. Agent-host queues are server-managed rather than eagerly drained by the client.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Capture new file contents before queueing, or account for already captured base64 data without rereading.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One content read per fresh clean file; zero content reads for existing snapshots. Exclusion checks still occur for URI-bearing entries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Queued file entries retained references without this submission-time snapshot.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks accepting the queued or steering message.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispatch ChatPendingMessageSet for changed pending messages, grouping that message's attachments.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Conditional dispatch per changed pending message, not per file. Existing reconciliation and equality checks remain in place.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same queue synchronization boundary; these file entries previously produced resource references.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The server cannot consume the queued attachment until its pending-message action is received.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Restore embedded document/selection payloads by retaining their existing base64 string rather than decoding them into generic byte entries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One small projection per embedded file attachment in received history or pending messages; no additional base64 decode is introduced here.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Embedded non-images were decoded to bytes and represented as generic entries; new document/selection projection preserves snapshot data.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Part of history/pending projection, with no new filesystem or network call.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Q pending messages, each with its own maximum 16 MiB device snapshots, and F file entries within the changed message. Pending-message conversion iterates the queue, while protocol dispatch is conditional on message changes.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Preparation is serial per send. _syncPendingMessages converts and compares queued messages synchronously, dispatching only changed ones. Server-managed queues do not repeatedly call the client send path merely to dequeue.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Captured snapshots survive reuse and bypass file reads and encoding. Restored snapshots without a URI also skip exclusion-provider calls. The client stores only metadata for external chat sessions, so full local chat-session serialization should not be assumed for this cloud path.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: queue acceptance order, snapshot fast path, conditional pending dispatch, server-managed dequeue guard, and history projection were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Queue length and attachment sizes are not measured; host rewriting and deployed cloud history behavior may vary. No independent new repeated-dispatch mechanism was proven.
Scenarios.Verdict: The preparation findings apply to fresh queued attachments. No additional finding for intentional snapshot retention, presumed per-file network fan-out, or presumed repeated full-history serialization.

Scenarios.Scenario: Send messages without device files, use existing image attachments, attach host-side resources, or use non-cloud/user-local connections.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The contribution flag and file-entry guards bypass snapshot preparation for unaffected sessions/messages. Host URI entries pass through prepare without local capture. Existing image handling remains unchanged.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing image attachment resolution may read image bytes. Host-scheme files are not read by the new device snapshot loop.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing image reads retain their previous cardinality; zero new local content reads for host-only files or messages bypassing preparation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same image-resolution implementation read image content; this diff does not alter it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Image resolution remains on its existing attachment path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing image and resource attachment dispatch; user-local customization does not require embedded device-file snapshots.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing grouped actions; no new per-file boundary on non-cloud/user-local paths.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same conversion and dispatch for entries without the new snapshot property.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Ordinary prompt parts and attachment counts. getPromptText now optionally searches attachment metadata for dynamic file references; no changed expensive-boundary multiplicity was established for these unaffected paths.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Unchanged outside the guarded cloud snapshot path. Prompt construction remains synchronous; no realistically significant new CPU regression was established from the metadata search alone.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No new cache or retention lifecycle on paths bypassing snapshot preparation. Existing host resource and image behavior is preserved.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for guard behavior and unchanged image/resource branches; no speculative renderer or serialization amplification was assumed.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No benchmark of prompt-part metadata searches was performed; ordinary attachment counts do not establish an actionable independent regression.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass across all 17 changed files and all diff pages against base 2219f59cf7c96358f40dac5a4aeda3fa7af85c6d. Submitted two concrete introduced regressions: unbounded native reads of rejected oversized attachments, and unreleased text-file models created for cold selection snapshots. Traced initial sends, draft handoff, queued/steering sends, snapshot/history reuse, and unaffected paths with boundary counts, caching, and concurrency. No high-confidence concrete performance-regression fix requiring blame provenance was identified. Read-only static analysis; deployed cloud-host implementation and measured timings were unavailable.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
